question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The actor decided to live life __in the fast lane__.
solution:
The correct answer is: **A life filled with excitement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"live life in the fast lane"** means to live a life filled with excitement and often risk. (उत्तेजना और जोखिम से भरा जीवन जीना)

 
 
• **Example:** Since becoming a celebrity, he has been **living life in the fast lane**, attending parties and traveling the world.
 
 
 
• **"Excitement"** refers to a feeling of great enthusiasm and eagerness. (उत्तेजना)
 
 
• **Example:** The **excitement **of the race was palpable among the spectators.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Dropping charges of crime** (अपराध के आरोपों को छोड़ना): To withdraw accusations or legal charges against someone.

 
 
• **Example:** The prosecutor decided to **drop the charges of crime** due to a lack of evidence.
 
 
 
• **Racing away to the moon** (चाँद की ओर दौड़ना): This phrase is not a common idiom and does not make contextual sense here.
 
 
• **Example:** The phrase "**racing away to the moon**" might be used in a poetic or imaginative context, but it does not apply to the given sentence.
 
 
 
• **A life of extreme speed** (अत्यधिक गति का जीवन): This could be interpreted similarly to "life in the fast lane," but it is not the most appropriate meaning in the given context.
 
 
• **Example:** Professional race car drivers live **a life of extreme speed**.
